sections.h2: South Salt Lake at a glance
sections.html:
South Salt Lake covers about 6.9 square miles directly below Salt Lake City, inside Salt Lake County. The Jordan River bounds it on the west, 500 East and 700 East on the east, 2100 South on the north and 3900 South on the south. In 2020 it held 26,777 people living in 10,448 households.

Renters outnumber owners here. Roughly 38 of every 100 occupied homes are lived in by their owners, which means plenty of sellers are landlords and the license and tenant issues below arise constantly.

Housing measureSouth Salt Lake, 2020 to 2024
Owner-occupied housing rate38.2%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$410,200
Median gross rent$1,451
Persons per household2.30
Median household income$72,152

Treat the median value as a survey figure, since condition, lot and location move a single house away from it. Granite School District covers the schools. For permits, code enforcement and business licenses, go to South Salt Lake City Hall at 220 East Morris Avenue.

sections.h2: Getting around: freeways, TRAX and the S Line
sections.html:
Buyers like the transit and the freeways. At the northwest corner is the Spaghetti Bowl, where I-15, I-80 and SR-201 come together, and both I-15 and I-80 have local interchanges.

  • TRAX light rail runs along roughly 200 West with three stations in the city, and the Blue, Red and Green lines meet at Central Pointe station.
  • The S Line streetcar opened in December 2013 and stops at Central Pointe, South Main, 300 East and 500 East.
  • The average commute is about 20 minutes.

Work out the walk from your address to the nearest stop. Buyers and tenants raise that distance almost immediately.

South Salt Lake polices yards, parked vehicles and property upkeep, and a first contact is usually a courtesy notice. Over 90% of issues end through conversation and education, but cases that drag on can bring fines and civil prosecution.

  • Lawns and ground cover must stay under 6 inches, and owners must control noxious weeds.
  • Vehicles belong on paved surfaces, not grass, dirt or gravel.
  • An inoperable or unregistered vehicle left 30 consecutive days is a public nuisance.
  • Trash bins go out by 7:00 a.m. on collection day and come back in afterward.
  • Sidewalks must be cleared of snow within 24 hours, leaving a path at least 42 inches wide.

An inherited house that was neglected may carry an open violation. Cleaning it up first takes one more worry off a buyer's list. The number to call about a specific property is 801-464-6757.

A landlord must hold a city license, and the Building Department and Fire Marshal inspect on site before one is issued. Renting without an approved license is a Class C misdemeanor.

Joining the Good Landlord Program means training every three years, written leases and background checks on adult occupants, and in return license fees drop significantly. A license cannot be transferred, so whoever buys a rental applies fresh.

For short-term stays, a pending ordinance issued October 15, 2026 stays in place for 180 days or until a new code is adopted. It defines a short-term rental as a stay under 30 consecutive days, requires an owner-occupied duplex, an owner-occupied rental or a property owned by a primary resident, and bars them in accessory dwelling units. Check the city's page for the final code before you plan on nightly rentals.

The county mails the bill and expects payment by November 30. On December 1 any unpaid current-year real property tax is delinquent, and the penalty is the greater of 2.5% or $10 per parcel. Pay in full by January 31 and it is cut to 1%.

A house you live in gets a 45% exemption, leaving 55% of market value taxable. Rentals and second homes get no such break, so an investment property's bill can look high.

The Treasurer is at 2001 S State St, Suite N1-200, and the Recorder, who files the deed, is in Suite N1-600 of the same building.

Notices of valuation go in the mail by July 22. Your window to appeal to the Board of Equalization ends September 15, or 45 days after the notice if that is later. Back your case with recent sales of comparable homes and photos or estimates showing condition problems the valuation overlooks.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in South Salt Lake
sections.html:
Bank underwriting never slows a cash buyer, a real plus for a house with put-off repairs or sitting tenants. Tell us the address, the condition and what you want from the sale, and a written offer follows.

The closing takes place at a title or escrow company, and the Salt Lake County Recorder records the deed. For a rental, settle lease, deposit and license questions with the buyer ahead of closing day, and provide every lease along with tenant payment records and any notices you sent. If the house is vacant, bring the keys, the utility account details and a list of anything left inside, so the handover is quick and nobody is surprised by what remains in the garage or basement.

sections.h2: Selling a rental house with tenants
sections.html:
Many sellers here own a rental, and a sale works best when the paperwork is ready. Tell the buyer up front whether the house is occupied, what each lease says and when it ends. Deposits belong to the tenants, so the title company needs to know where they are held and who takes responsibility for them after closing.

Because the city license does not move to a new owner, a buyer who plans to keep renting must pass the inspections and apply on their own. A buyer who plans to live in the house or renovate it has a different timeline. Knowing which kind of buyer you have shapes the closing date you can offer.

Ask the title company for a closing statement ahead of time. It lists the tax split, any payoff and the recording charge, so you can see what you will receive before you sign.

If the rental license has lapsed or an inspection was failed, fix what you can before showing the house, or tell the cash buyer so the offer reflects it.

sections.h2: Checks to run before you accept an offer
sections.html:
• Does every unit in a duplex or converted basement have a building permit on file?
  • Is the rental license current, and were the inspections passed?
  • Is any code complaint open about weeds, vehicles or trash?
  • Who lives in the house, and must a lease or deposit transfer?

If a cash buyer hears these answers first, the offer comes out cleaner and late renegotiation becomes unlikely.

faqs.q: Which county is South Salt Lake in?
faqs.a: Salt Lake County. Its Assessor values your house, its Treasurer collects the tax and its Recorder files your deed.

faqs.q: When is South Salt Lake property tax due?
faqs.a: By November 30. After that the current-year tax is delinquent from December 1, with a lower 1% penalty for payment in full by January 31.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent out my South Salt Lake house?
faqs.a: Yes, and inspections by the Building Department and Fire Marshal come first. Renting without a license is a Class C misdemeanor, and Good Landlord certification cuts the fee.

faqs.q: Can I run a short-term rental in South Salt Lake?
faqs.a: Only under the pending ordinance issued October 15, 2026, which covers owner-occupied or primary-resident properties and bans ADUs. Check the city page for the final code.

faqs.q: How much is a house worth in South Salt Lake?
faqs.a: The median value of owner-occupied homes is $410,200 for 2020 to 2024. That is a survey median, and your own house may sit above or below it.
